## SCHOLARLY + DS&A CONTEXT
# ALGORITHM: IRT 2PL calibration (Joint Maximum Likelihood Estimation)
#   source:      journey-os-algorithms-scholarly.html §III · IRT specification
#   complexity:  O(n * m * k) where n=items, m=students, k=iterations (typically k<50)
#   parameters:
#     - Minimum responses per item: 30 (statistical reliability threshold)
#     - a (discrimination): initialized at 1.0, constrained to [0.2, 3.0]
#     - b (difficulty): initialized at 0.0, constrained to [-4.0, 4.0]
#     - Convergence: |delta_a| < 0.001 AND |delta_b| < 0.001
#     - Max iterations: 50
#   security:    N/A
#   invariants:
#     - Only items with >=30 responses are calibrated
#     - Calibrated parameters written to item_irt_params table (Supabase-first)
#     - Uncalibrated items keep defaults (a=1.0, b=0.0) — never partially calibrated
#     - Calibration NEVER modifies p_mastery or student theta directly
#
# FOUNDATION: Lord, 1980
#   claim:   IRT 2PL requires >=30 responses per item for stable parameter estimates
#   rule:    Skip items with < 30 responses; they keep uncalibrated defaults
#   applies: apps/inngest/functions/cron-weekly-calibrate.ts

## Summary
Build a weekly Inngest cron job that recalibrates IRT 2PL parameters (discrimination and difficulty) for assessment items that have accumulated at least 30 student responses, replacing uncalibrated defaults with empirically estimated values.

## User story
As the system, I want to recalibrate item parameters weekly based on accumulated response data, so that the practice session builder selects items with increasingly accurate difficulty and discrimination estimates.

## Why this matters
IRT-based adaptive practice is only as good as its item parameters. Starting with uncalibrated defaults (a=1.0, b=0.0) is acceptable for cold-start, but after 30+ responses, empirical calibration dramatically improves item selection accuracy. Without calibration, the practice builder treats all items as equally discriminating and equally difficult.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Inngest cron fires weekly on Monday at 2am: `"cron": "0 2 * * 1"`
- [ ] Only items with >= 30 responses are calibrated
- [ ] 2PL estimation converges within 50 iterations (|delta| < 0.001)
- [ ] Discrimination (a) constrained to [0.2, 3.0]
- [ ] Difficulty (b) constrained to [-4.0, 4.0]
- [ ] Calibrated params written to item_irt_params table (Supabase-first, Rule 6)
- [ ] Items with < 30 responses are untouched (keep defaults a=1.0, b=0.0)
- [ ] Calibration is idempotent — running twice produces same result
- [ ] Batch calibration uses Promise.allSettled (Rule 3)
- [ ] Calibration log records: items_calibrated, items_skipped, convergence_failures

## Canonical decisions in play
| Rule | What it means for this story |
|---|---|
| Rule 3 (AP-03) | Promise.allSettled for batch item calibration |
| Rule 6 (G08) | Supabase-first: write item_irt_params to Supabase, Neo4j sync optional |
| Rule 11 (C03) | Atomic upsert for item_irt_params — no read-modify-write |

## Schema changes
```sql
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS public.item_irt_params (
  id UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
  item_id UUID NOT NULL UNIQUE,
  discrimination DOUBLE PRECISION NOT NULL DEFAULT 1.0,
  difficulty DOUBLE PRECISION NOT NULL DEFAULT 0.0,
  guessing DOUBLE PRECISION NOT NULL DEFAULT 0.20,
  response_count INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
  calibrated BOOLEAN NOT NULL DEFAULT false,
  last_calibrated_at TIMESTAMPTZ,
  convergence_iterations INTEGER,
  created_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
  updated_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now()
);

CREATE INDEX idx_item_irt_params_calibrated
  ON public.item_irt_params (calibrated, response_count DESC);

ALTER TABLE public.item_irt_params ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY;
CREATE POLICY "Authenticated users can read IRT params"
  ON public.item_irt_params FOR SELECT
  USING (auth.uid() IS NOT NULL);

-- Atomic upsert for calibrated params
CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION public.upsert_irt_params(
  p_item_id UUID,
  p_discrimination DOUBLE PRECISION,
  p_difficulty DOUBLE PRECISION,
  p_response_count INTEGER,
  p_convergence_iterations INTEGER
) RETURNS public.item_irt_params AS $$
  INSERT INTO public.item_irt_params (item_id, discrimination, difficulty, response_count, calibrated, last_calibrated_at, convergence_iterations)
  VALUES (p_item_id, p_discrimination, p_difficulty, p_response_count, true, now(), p_convergence_iterations)
  ON CONFLICT (item_id) DO UPDATE SET
    discrimination = p_discrimination,
    difficulty = p_difficulty,
    response_count = p_response_count,
    calibrated = true,
    last_calibrated_at = now(),
    convergence_iterations = p_convergence_iterations,
    updated_at = now()
  RETURNING *;
$$ LANGUAGE sql;

-- After adding: pnpm db:types to regenerate database.generated.ts
```

## Inngest event context
Function: journey/cron-weekly-calibrate
Trigger: `"cron": "0 2 * * 1"` (Monday 2am)
Step 1: step.run('find-calibration-candidates', ...) — items with >= 30 responses, not calibrated this week
Step 2: step.run('fetch-response-matrices', ...) — load response data per item
Step 3: step.run('calibrate-items', ...) — Promise.allSettled across items, 2PL JMLE
Step 4: step.run('write-calibrated-params', ...) — atomic upsert via Supabase RPC
Emits: journey/cron.weekly-calibrate { items_calibrated, items_skipped, convergence_failures }
onFailure: Log to dead letter queue, retry next week (stale params are acceptable)

## API contract
```
None — this is an Inngest cron function, not an API route.
Practice builder (E08-S05) reads item_irt_params at session creation time:
  supabase.from('item_irt_params').select().eq('item_id', itemId)
  Falls back to defaults (a=1.0, b=0.0, c=0.20) if no row exists.
```

## Code patterns to follow
```typescript
// features/mastery-tracking/services/IrtCalibrationService.ts
export const CALIBRATION_CONSTRAINTS = {
  min_responses: 30,
  a_min: 0.2,
  a_max: 3.0,
  b_min: -4.0,
  b_max: 4.0,
  convergence_threshold: 0.001,
  max_iterations: 50,
} as const;

/**
 * IRT 2PL Joint Maximum Likelihood Estimation
 * Estimates discrimination (a) and difficulty (b) from response matrix
 */
export function calibrate2PL(
  responses: Array<{ theta: number; correct: boolean }>
): { a: number; b: number; iterations: number; converged: boolean } {
  let a = 1.0;
  let b = 0.0;
  let converged = false;
  let iterations = 0;

  for (let i = 0; i < CALIBRATION_CONSTRAINTS.max_iterations; i++) {
    iterations = i + 1;

    // E-step: compute expected scores given current params
    // M-step: update a and b using Newton-Raphson
    const { newA, newB } = newtonRaphsonStep(a, b, responses);

    // Constrain parameters
    const clampedA = Math.max(CALIBRATION_CONSTRAINTS.a_min,
      Math.min(CALIBRATION_CONSTRAINTS.a_max, newA));
    const clampedB = Math.max(CALIBRATION_CONSTRAINTS.b_min,
      Math.min(CALIBRATION_CONSTRAINTS.b_max, newB));

    // Check convergence
    if (Math.abs(clampedA - a) < CALIBRATION_CONSTRAINTS.convergence_threshold &&
        Math.abs(clampedB - b) < CALIBRATION_CONSTRAINTS.convergence_threshold) {
      converged = true;
      a = clampedA;
      b = clampedB;
      break;
    }

    a = clampedA;
    b = clampedB;
  }

  return { a, b, iterations, converged };
}

// apps/inngest/functions/cron-weekly-calibrate.ts

export const cronWeeklyCalibrate = inngest.createFunction(
  { id: 'cron-weekly-calibrate', retries: 1 },
  { cron: '0 2 * * 1' },
  async ({ step }) => {
    const candidates = await step.run('find-calibration-candidates', async () => {
      // items with >= 30 responses
    });

    const results = await step.run('calibrate-items', async () => {
      // Promise.allSettled across candidates (Rule 3)
      return Promise.allSettled(
        candidates.map(item => calibrateItem(item))
      );
    });

    await step.run('write-calibrated-params', async () => {
      // Atomic upsert via supabase.rpc('upsert_irt_params', ...)
    });
  }
);
```

## Code patterns to AVOID
```typescript
// ✗ AP-03: Promise.all for batch calibration
await Promise.all(items.map(i => calibrate(i))); // BANNED
// ✓ Use: Promise.allSettled(items.map(i => calibrate(i)));

// ✗ Calibrating items with insufficient data
if (responses.length > 0) { calibrate(item); } // BANNED — need >= 30
// ✓ Use: if (responses.length >= CALIBRATION_CONSTRAINTS.min_responses)

// ✗ Unconstrained parameters
return { a: newA, b: newB }; // BANNED — could produce extreme values
// ✓ Use: clamp a to [0.2, 3.0], b to [-4.0, 4.0]

// ✗ Read-modify-write for IRT params
const params = await supabase.from('item_irt_params').select().single();
params.discrimination = newA;
await supabase.from('item_irt_params').update(params); // BANNED
// ✓ Use: supabase.rpc('upsert_irt_params', { ... })
```

## Automated tests (Playwright — runs during /validate)
```typescript
// tests/E08/E08-S09.pipeline.test.ts
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';
import {
  calibrate2PL,
  CALIBRATION_CONSTRAINTS,
} from '../../features/mastery-tracking/services/IrtCalibrationService';

test('2PL calibration: easy item (80% correct) has negative difficulty', () => {
  const responses = Array(40).fill(null).map((_, i) => ({
    theta: (i - 20) / 5, // spread across -4 to +4
    correct: Math.random() < 0.80,
  }));
  const { b, converged } = calibrate2PL(responses);
  expect(b).toBeLessThan(0); // easy items have negative difficulty
  expect(converged).toBe(true);
});

test('2PL calibration: hard item (30% correct) has positive difficulty', () => {
  const responses = Array(40).fill(null).map((_, i) => ({
    theta: (i - 20) / 5,
    correct: Math.random() < 0.30,
  }));
  const { b, converged } = calibrate2PL(responses);
  expect(b).toBeGreaterThan(0); // hard items have positive difficulty
  expect(converged).toBe(true);
});

test('2PL calibration: discrimination constrained to [0.2, 3.0]', () => {
  const responses = Array(50).fill(null).map((_, i) => ({
    theta: (i - 25) / 6,
    correct: i > 25, // perfect step function — would produce extreme a
  }));
  const { a } = calibrate2PL(responses);
  expect(a).toBeGreaterThanOrEqual(CALIBRATION_CONSTRAINTS.a_min);
  expect(a).toBeLessThanOrEqual(CALIBRATION_CONSTRAINTS.a_max);
});

test('2PL calibration: difficulty constrained to [-4.0, 4.0]', () => {
  // All correct — would push b to -infinity without constraint
  const responses = Array(30).fill({ theta: 0, correct: true });
  const { b } = calibrate2PL(responses);
  expect(b).toBeGreaterThanOrEqual(CALIBRATION_CONSTRAINTS.b_min);
  expect(b).toBeLessThanOrEqual(CALIBRATION_CONSTRAINTS.b_max);
});

test('2PL calibration: converges within 50 iterations', () => {
  const responses = Array(40).fill(null).map((_, i) => ({
    theta: (i - 20) / 5,
    correct: Math.random() < 0.55, // near chance
  }));
  const { iterations } = calibrate2PL(responses);
  expect(iterations).toBeLessThanOrEqual(CALIBRATION_CONSTRAINTS.max_iterations);
});

test('Minimum response threshold is 30', () => {
  expect(CALIBRATION_CONSTRAINTS.min_responses).toBe(30);
});
```
